Let clothing, hair, props, furniture, tools, weather, architecture, and nearby surfaces respond to the same forces through pressure, contact, scale, and perspective.

records.label: Anthropomorphic animal character realization
records.realization_promise: Translate the art direction into an upright animal-derived character whose species identity, humanoid body logic, individual morphology, permanent hair and fur distribution, facial performance, posture, clothing, hands or paws, and tail form one coherent design.
records.identity_and_silhouette: Preserve a species-bearing muzzle or beak structure, ears or other head appendages, tail, feet, hands or paws, body ratios, head hair, mane, facial furnishings, coat distribution, markings, and distinctive individual features, carried on a humanoid torso and limbs with species-appropriate lower legs and one coherent tail or caudal structure. Muzzle or beak mass follows the body's build, a heavyset frame carrying a thick deep muzzle and a lean frame a short slim one, with facial dimensions anchored to landmarks outside themselves such as the eye.
records.performance_channels: Use eyes, gaze target, eyelids, brows or brow-equivalent shapes, ears or head appendages, muzzle or beak corners, tongue, jaw, cheek flush, whiskers, ruff or hackles, head angle and pitch, shoulders, hands or paws, claws, stance, feet, tail, breath, contact, and distance together. A performance record selects the meaning from the combined channel pattern and scene context, so a tongue display, blush, ear angle, or tail motion remains one cue inside the full read.
records.anatomy_and_weight: Join animal-derived head and extremity structures to an upright load-bearing skeleton, preserve readable joints and hand construction, distribute muscle and soft tissue coherently beneath the surface, and ground feet or paws through believable contact on humanoid or digitigrade legs according to the design.
records.surface_and_materials: Separate scalp-like head hair, mane, cheek or jaw furnishings, short and long body fur regions, bare pads or skin, claws, clothing, and accessories through controlled texture, grouping fur, feathers, scales, hide, exposed skin, prosthetics, or mixed species surfaces into deliberate systems appropriate to the chosen medium. The main body coat keeps continuous color and marking paths across the visible head, torso, limbs, hands or paws, and tail. A separately declared hairstyle, mane, feather crest, scale plate region, exposed-skin region, prosthetic, plush coat, long-pile coat, painterly coat, or other explicit surface system keeps its own palette, texture, and finish while meeting adjacent systems at designed anatomical boundaries. Across style families, fur-bearing regions use one anatomical contour-distribution rule modulated by the selected surface state. A shaved region, very short slick coat, saturated or compressed fur, or tightly groomed hair yields a nearly continuous contour; a fuller free coat allows more breaks. Keep long straight and gently curved outer-contour runs mostly continuous. Concentrate silhouette breaks where anatomical curvature changes abruptly: at convex points of strongly bent joints, at ruff or mass transitions, and at visible concave contour junctions between volumes. The selected style family and explicit surface presets set the break count, depth, strand visibility, edge sharpness, and gloss behavior. Clothing, leather, metal, water, bedding, and props remain visibly separate materials with their own construction and contact response.
records.viewer_relationship: Select viewer contact, partner attention, or environmental focus from the scene, then coordinate eyes, gaze target, ears or appendage attitude, muzzle or beak direction and tension, head turn, torso, hands, tail, and personal distance to establish social distance and emotional intent.
records.motion_and_environment: Use humanoid reach, grip, seating, clothing, and tool interaction while preserving species-specific balance, lower-leg construction, tail clearance, and environmental contact. Let fur masses, head hair, mane, tail, clothing, and accessories respond to gravity and motion, and let furniture and props accommodate the body plan while the body establishes clear weight, balance, and contact.
